en.title: Ocarina of Time Remake Already Breached by Speedrunners, New Glitches Emerge
en.summary: Just days after its November 5, 2026 release, the Nintendo Switch 2 remake of **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time** is already being deconstructed by dedicated speedrunners. Early discoveries hint at game-breaking exploits that could redefine existing records.
en.body:
The release of **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time** on Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5, 2026, was met with widespread acclaim, celebrating a beloved classic with modern enhancements like fully voiced cutscenes and the long-requested jump button. However, for the game's most dedicated fans, the true excitement often lies not just in replaying the adventure, but in dissecting its very code for new shortcuts and exploits. It appears this new remake is no exception, as speedrunners have wasted no time in finding ways to bend and break the Hyrule of their childhood.

Barely days into the remake's life cycle, players are already uncovering physics exploits that allow for unprecedented movement. Reports indicate that Link can be launched into the air at extreme speeds, a tactic that, with careful positioning and a safe landing, can bypass significant portions of the game. This phenomenon, observed by prominent speedrunners like ZFG and shared by others on social media, suggests that the game's engine, even in its updated form, harbors secrets ripe for exploitation. The potential for skipping entire dungeons or boss encounters through these aerial maneuvers is immense, promising to shake up established speedrunning categories.

## The Speedrunning Crucible

This rapid discovery of glitches is a testament to the speedrunning community's unparalleled dedication and technical prowess. For decades, **Ocarina of Time** has been a cornerstone of the speedrunning world, accumulating a vast lexicon of complex tricks and sequence breaks. The remake, with its fresh coat of paint and underlying engine, presents a new, uncharted territory for these players. The immediate identification of high-speed launch glitches is just the tip of the iceberg, as the community will undoubtedly continue to probe every corner of the game for more advanced strategies.

## Implications for the Community

For fans who follow speedrunning, these early discoveries are thrilling. They represent the birth of new categories and strategies for a game they thought they knew inside and out. The ability to perform what were once impossible feats, or to find entirely novel ways to progress, keeps the game fresh and exciting. It’s a constant race against time and code, where ingenuity and persistence are rewarded with world records. The implications for future runs are significant, potentially leading to drastically shorter completion times and entirely new routing strategies that were unimaginable before.

## What's Next

As the community continues to explore the **Ocarina of Time** remake, more glitches and exploits are almost certainly waiting to be found. We can expect to see new world records emerge as runners perfect these discovered techniques and uncover even more groundbreaking strategies in the coming weeks and months.

content_raw: From quicker movement to sending Link to space, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time speedrunners have already found a few ways to break the remake. One of the best things about a new Zelda game is seeing just how quickly players can speed through it, but Nintendo's latest video game being a remake presents a unique situation. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has accumulated some of the most bizarre speedrunning strategies in its 28 years on the market, and in just a few days, the Nintendo Switch 2 remake looks like it will live up to that legacy. Creative players started peeling back the layers of the new version of Link and Zelda's classic adventure just hours after it launched November 5. Even just moments into its life, they've discovered some seemingly useful (and hilarious) ways to break the game, with more almost certainly to be discovered in the weeks, months, and years ahead. Let's start with what might be the most common tactic under investigation so far: sending Link hurdling into the air at high speed. Ocarina of Time Remake speedrunning has begun — ZFG (@zfg111) November 7, 2026 Ocarina of Time speedrunner Zfg1 seems to be one of the first to discover that the Switch 2 Zelda remake has interesting physics, which, if pushed far enough, can toss Link into the air like a firework. Even at first glance, you can probably guess how a safe landing from that height opens the door for players to get creative and skip portions of the game. It seems relatively easy to replicate, too, with X/Twitter user @Vespher also sharing footage of them pulling off the same stunt in the same location. Other locations seem to be susceptible to Link's sudden weightlessness with some careful positioning, with a similar area highlighted by other players . You might think that Link will only be able to fling himself skyward in extremely specific locations, but fear not, as there are other ways to send him for a ride. Another popular glitch making the rounds in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake's first weekend in the public's hands only asks Hyrule's hero to stand in a chest. A few sudden movements (or even a well-placed bomb), and poof, ceiling. Whether it's walking backward, hopping, or rolling, there are plenty of different ways to get around Hyrule.
